# Keys you hand over - qa-case-critic

## Outputs

- `work/test-cases/critic-findings.md` - the S4 critic's findings live beside the cases they review, one file per area and round; listed before the directory below so the designer's directory does not claim them

Required at your stop (stage S4): `work/test-cases/`.
Re-run by the gate at your stop: `critic_rollcall.py`, `branch_accounting.py`.

## Witness

Your witness artifact (stages.json `witness`): `state/story-case-links.json`.

## Handoff form

Contract `s4-case-critic-to-designer` (fill `work/handoffs/<dispatch>.yaml`; `handoff_check.py` reads it):

- `inputs_read[].version` (optional) - the pinned cv_ id, or the file's sha256
- `header.window` (required) - the case ids under review
- `header.verdict` (required) - one of vocabulary.header_verdicts
- `review.outcome` (required) - one of vocabulary.critic_verdicts
- `review.rollcall` (required) - n of m reviewed - the number critic_rollcall.py computed, never typed
- `review.rounds_used` (required) - which round of the two this was
- `review.rubric_covered` (required) - the dimensions of the eight actually applied, by name
- `scope[].id` (required) - case id
- `scope[].state` (required) - one of vocabulary.row_states
- `scope[].reason` (required) - a verdict of at most 80 characters - the explanation lives in the artifact
- `scope[].case_version` (required) - the pinned version reviewed
- `findings[].id` (required) - F-n
- `findings[].case` (required) - case id
- `findings[].where` (optional) - the section or step of the case, or a line
- `findings[].problem` (required) - what is wrong, one sentence
- `findings[].expected` (required) - what the reviewer expects to see instead, concretely - the Then line, the precondition, the oracle, the value
- `findings[].fix` (required) - what to do, one sentence
- `findings[].check` (optional) - what shows the author it is satisfied, or a dash when nothing does
- `findings[].dimension` (required) - the rubric dimension this comes from
- `findings[].blocking` (required) - true|false
- `findings[].replacement.old` (optional) - the exact text to replace, or omit the block entirely
- `findings[].replacement.new` (required) - the exact text to put there
- `unverified[].id` (required) - case id
- `unverified[].why` (required) - one sentence: what stopped the proof
- `unverified[].expected` (required) - what the review wanted to see, so the author knows whether it can supply it
- `unverified[].would_settle_it` (required) - what evidence or access would
- `stage_acceptance.failure_class` (required) - spec|capability|data|tooling
- `stage_acceptance.quote` (required) - the artifact's own words, with path#anchor
- `stage_acceptance.witness_paths[]` (optional) - task-relative path the verdict rests on, or omit when the acceptor cited no evidence paths
- `not_looked[].where` (required) - path or area
- `not_looked[].why` (required) - one sentence
- `advice_read` (optional) - each advice file the brief names - work/advice-S4.json, work/advice-S2.json, work/advice-S3.json - read, or a dash and the reason it was absent
- `advice_rejected[].script` (required) - the adviser
- `advice_rejected[].why` (required) - one sentence: why its remark is not a defect
- `questions[].question` (required) - the question, in plain words
- `questions[].read[]` (required) - path#anchor the critic read before asking
- `questions[].recommendation` (required) - what the work goes on with meanwhile
- `questions[].options[].reading` (required) - one possible answer
- `questions[].options[].if_chosen` (required) - what changes in the work if this is the answer
- `questions[].severity` (required) - blocker|major|minor
- `questions[].owner_role` (required) - the role the answer concerns
- `questions[].why_person` (optional) - the class of person-owned.json, or omit when none
- `register_gaps[].title` (required) - the gap in one line
- `register_gaps[].statement` (required) - the register line and what no requirement holds
- `register_gaps[].refs[]` (optional) - R-n or TC-n the gap stands against, or omit
- `register_gaps[].missing_prerequisite` (required) - what would close it: a requirement or an answer
- `claims.every_case_of_the_review_scope_has_a_row` (required) - true|false
- `claims.every_finding_names_expected_and_check` (required) - true|false
- `claims.the_verdict_was_computed_by_rollcall_not_typed` (required) - true|false
- `claims.no_case_outside_the_review_scope_was_reviewed` (required) - true|false
- `blocked.field` (only when blocked) - the field of this file the role cannot fill
- `blocked.problem` (only when blocked) - what the role tried and what refused it, verbatim
- `blocked.tried[]` (only when blocked) - command or step, and its answer
- `blocked.data[]` (only when blocked) - path of anything the conductor needs to see

Every handoff form shares one skeleton (`common_shape` of handoffs/index.yaml): `inputs`, `inputs_read`, `header`, `scope`, `artifacts`, `claims`, `unresolved`, `blocked`.

## What code will check of you

`<T>` is your ticket, `<ID>` your dispatch id, `<home>` the project's qa-factory folder - all three stand in your prompt (`Ticket: ... Dispatch: ...`) and in your task packet.

- [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] Your final message is the handoff form: a header `<role> <stage> <window> · ok|concerns|halt|impossible`; one line `<id> · <state> · <reason of at most 80 characters>` for every item of the dispatch's scope (a halting digest owes no scope lines); nothing but those lines between the header and the path; and, last, the task-relative path of what you wrote (a halting digest may omit it). Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [exit_gate:EG-text-end] Your dispatch ends with the host's handback tool carrying your digest line, never with free text after it. Door: call the host's handback tool with your digest line.
- [handoff_check:blocked_problem] A row in state `blocked` carries `blocked.problem`; `blocked_by_env` is used only where `options_for_role` offers it to this role. Door: write the problem, or pick a state the role is offered.
- [handoff_check:claims] What the form claims is true is true on disk ("the form claims this is true, and it is not"). Door: fix the claim or make it true.
- [handoff_check:cli] The call names an existing UTF-8 form with a `contract:` line and an existing values file; `--shorten` only with `--fix`. Door: the refusal's door; a non-UTF-8 form: run `handoff_init` again.
- [handoff_check:field.blank] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write the value as a `path: value` line in the values file, then run the check again.
- [handoff_check:field.max_len] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: shorten it (`--shorten` with `--fix`) or rewrite.
- [handoff_check:field.value] every `required` field of your handoff form (section `Handoff form` of this page). Door: write one of the listed words (or `new: <word> -- <why>` where the list is open).
- [handoff_check:required_rows] A required list has one row per item in scope: the id, a state and a reason of at most 80 characters. Door: write the rows as index lines in the values file, then run this check again.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.null_word] A list's null-outcome word (the declared empty outcome) stands only when the list has no rows; never both. Door: remove the word or remove the rows.
- [handoff_check:required_rows.owed_by_verdict] When the verdict owes rows (the verdict word names work done on items), the list is not empty. Door: write the rows the verdict owes, or change the verdict.
- [handoff_check:values_apply] Each path names a field of this contract, by its index where it is a list row, not a contract-owned path; a list field gets a list and a one-value field one value; rows open in order. Door: correct the path (the refusal suggests "did you mean").
- [handoff_check:values_file] The values file is `path: value` lines (or a JSON object): valid JSON, an object not a list, each path given once, each key a field path, no nested value. Door: fix the line the refusal names (FILE_FIX).
- [exit_gate:digest] Your final message has the digest form stated in the row [exit_gate:EG-digest-form] of this section. Door: fix the digest line the refusal names, then end the dispatch again.
- [guard_pre_tool:*] 17 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.
- [host_adapter:*] 7 checks of your tool calls are told in the refusal of the call, with what they expect and the door; nothing you have written is lost by them.

### Not yet in rows

critic_rollcall.py computes your verdict from your own findings file at the exit gate. A `## Roll-call` table with one row per case in scope, and give it a column headed `reviewed` holding yes or no. A `Verdict:` line from approve|approve_with_fixes|approve_with_concerns|partial|reject. If any row is not reviewed, an approving verdict is refused: the verdict that roll-call computes is `partial`, your digest must say '<n> of <m> reviewed', and an `Unreviewed for Gate A:` line must name every unreviewed case. A concern of the last round that comes with an exact replacement is applied by code: put those in a fenced JSON array under `## Fixes without a new round`, each object carrying case_id, locator, find, replace and reviewed_version. `approve_with_fixes` without that block is refused, and so is that block beside any other verdict. Cases sharing an R-n: a row per pair under `## Merge candidates` (cases | verdict merge|keep | reason; keep starts P16 or P19); merge: each case `approve_with_concerns`, note `parametrise into one test: <ids>`. e2e-ui/manual row notes: `lower level: <level|impossible> - <why>`. Over the plan case budget: an `Over the plan case budget:` line.
